FAQ’s Related to Treatments 
 
PROCTOLOGY (Piles, Fissure, Fistula, Pilonidal) 
 
1. What are piles (hemorrhoids)? 
Piles are swollen vascular cushions inside or around the anal canal that can cause bleeding, pain, and swelling. 
2. What causes piles? 
Chronic constipation, straining during stool, prolonged sitting, pregnancy, obesity, and low-fiber diet. 
3. Is bleeding during stool always piles? 
No. Bleeding can also be due to fissure, fistula, polyps, or colorectal disease. Proper evaluation is necessary. 
4. How are piles diagnosed? 
Through physical examination, digital rectal exam, and proctoscopy. 
5. What are the different grades of piles? 
Grade 1 (bleeding only) to Grade 4 (permanent prolapse). 
6. Can piles heal without surgery? 
Early-stage piles can improve with medicines, diet, and lifestyle changes. 
7. What foods should I avoid in piles? 
Low-fiber foods, junk food, processed food, and excessive spicy food. 
8. Does spicy food cause piles? 
It does not directly cause piles but may worsen symptoms. 
9. Is laser treatment safe for piles? 
Yes, laser is safe, minimally invasive, and reduces pain and recovery time. 
10. How long does piles surgery take? 
Usually 20–40 minutes. 
11. Is piles surgery painful? 
Laser procedures cause minimal discomfort compared to open surgery. 
12. How many days rest is needed after piles surgery? 
Most patients resume routine work within 3–5 days. 
13. Can piles come back after surgery? 
Recurrence is rare if lifestyle changes are maintained. 
14. What is stapler surgery for piles? 
A technique that removes excess prolapsed tissue using a circular stapling device. 
15. What is the difference between laser and open surgery? 
Laser involves minimal cuts and faster healing; open surgery has longer recovery. 
16. Is piles common during pregnancy? 
Yes, due to increased abdominal pressure. 
17. Can sitting for long hours cause piles? 
Prolonged sitting can worsen symptoms. 
18. Does constipation worsen piles? 
Yes, straining increases pressure in anal veins. 
19. Are external piles more painful? 
Yes, because they have pain-sensitive nerve supply. 
20. When should I see a doctor for piles? 
If bleeding, severe pain, or prolapse occurs. 
21. What is an anal fissure? 
A small tear in the lining of the anal canal. 
22. What causes fissure? 
Hard stool, constipation, childbirth, chronic diarrhea. 
23. Why is fissure pain severe? 
Due to exposure of nerve endings in the anal lining. 
24. Can fissure heal with medicines? 
Acute fissures often heal with medication and stool softeners. 

25. What is laser fissure surgery? 
A minimally invasive procedure to relax the anal muscle and promote healing. 
26. What is lateral internal sphincterotomy? 
A minor surgical procedure that reduces anal muscle spasm. 
27. Is fissure surgery permanent? 
Yes, success rate is very high. 
28. How long does fissure recovery take? 
Usually 5–7 days for routine activity. 
29. What is an anal fistula? 
An abnormal tunnel between the anal canal and skin. 
30. How does fistula develop? 
Due to infection of anal glands. 
31. Is fistula dangerous? 
It can cause repeated infection if untreated. 
32. Can fistula heal without surgery? 
Usually no; surgery is required. 
33. What is laser fistula treatment (FiLaC)? 
Laser closure of the fistula tract without major cuts. 
34. What is VAAFT procedure? 
Video-assisted technique to treat fistula internally. 
35. What is the recurrence rate of fistula? 
Low when treated properly with advanced techniques. 
36. How long is hospital stay for fistula surgery? 
Often same-day or 24 hours. 
37. What is pilonidal sinus? 
A sinus tract near the tailbone containing hair and debris. 
38. What causes pilonidal sinus? 
Ingrown hair and infection. 
39. Is pilonidal sinus common in young males? 
Yes, especially those who sit long hours. 
40. What is laser treatment for pilonidal sinus? 
Laser destroys the infected tract with minimal incision. 
41. Is pilonidal surgery permanent? 
Yes, if completely treated. 
42. How soon can I sit after surgery? 
Usually within 1–2 days depending on procedure. 
43. Are these procedures covered under insurance? 
Most are covered, subject to policy terms. 
44. Is same-day discharge possible? 
Yes, in most laser cases. 
45. Can I travel after surgery? 
Short travel is usually possible within a few days. 
46. What precautions should I follow after surgery? 
High-fiber diet, hydration, hygiene, avoid straining. 
47. What complications can occur if untreated? 
Chronic pain, infection, bleeding, anemia. 
48. Can these conditions cause anemia? 
Chronic bleeding piles can lead to anemia. 
49. Is surgery done under local or spinal anesthesia? 
Usually spinal or short general anesthesia.

LAPAROSCOPIC SURGERY 
 
1. What is laparoscopic surgery? 
It is a minimally invasive surgical technique performed using small incisions and a camera (laparoscope). 
2. How is laparoscopic surgery different from open surgery? 
Laparoscopy uses small cuts, causes less pain, and allows faster recovery compared to larger open incisions. 
3. Is laparoscopic surgery safe? 
Yes, it is widely practiced and considered very safe when performed by experienced surgeons. 
4. What are the advantages of minimally invasive surgery? 
Less pain, minimal scars, shorter hospital stay, and quicker return to routine life. 
5. How long does laparoscopic surgery take? 
Usually 30 minutes to 2 hours depending on the procedure. 
6. Is general anesthesia required? 
Most laparoscopic surgeries are performed under general anesthesia. 
7. How many stitches are needed in laparoscopy? 
Typically 2–4 small stitches. 
8. Is laparoscopic surgery painful? 
Pain is usually mild and manageable with medication. 
9. How many days rest is required after laparoscopy? 
Most patients resume normal activities within 3–7 days. 
10. Can laparoscopic surgery fail? 
Rarely, but sometimes conversion to open surgery may be needed for safety. 
11. What is a hernia? 
A hernia is a bulge caused by weakness in the abdominal wall. 
12. What causes hernia? 
Heavy lifting, chronic cough, obesity, pregnancy, or muscle weakness. 
13. Is hernia dangerous if untreated? 
Yes, it can lead to obstruction or strangulation of intestine. 
14. Can hernia heal without surgery? 
No, surgery is the only permanent solution. 
15. What is laparoscopic hernia repair? 
A procedure where mesh is placed through small incisions to strengthen the abdominal wall. 
16. Is mesh used in hernia surgery? 
Yes, mesh reinforces the weak area and reduces recurrence. 
17. Is hernia surgery permanent? 
Yes, recurrence is low with proper repair. 
18. How long is hospital stay for hernia surgery? 
Usually same-day discharge or 24 hours. 
19. What is gallstone disease? 
Formation of stones inside the gallbladder. 
20. What causes gallstones? 
Cholesterol imbalance, obesity, rapid weight loss, or genetics. 
21. Do all gallstones require surgery? 
No, only symptomatic stones need removal. 
22. What are symptoms of gallstones? 
Upper abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, bloating. 
23. What is laparoscopic cholecystectomy? 
Removal of the gallbladder using laparoscopic technique. 
24. Can gallstones come back after surgery? 
No, because the gallbladder is removed. 
25. Is gallbladder removal safe? 
Yes, people live normally without a gallbladder. 

26. What is appendicitis? 
Inflammation of the appendix. 
27. What are symptoms of appendix infection? 
Right lower abdominal pain, fever, nausea. 
28. Is appendix surgery an emergency? 
Yes, untreated appendix can rupture. 
29. What is laparoscopic appendectomy? 
Removal of appendix through small incisions. 
30. How long does appendix recovery take? 
Most patients recover in 1–2 weeks. 
31. What is hydrocele? 
Fluid collection around the testicle. 
32. What causes hydrocele? 
Injury, infection, or inflammation. 
33. Is hydrocele painful? 
Usually painless but may cause swelling discomfort. 
34. Can hydrocele resolve on its own? 
In adults, surgery is often required. 
35. What is hydrocelectomy? 
Surgical removal of hydrocele fluid sac. 
36. Is hydrocele surgery done under local or general anesthesia? 
Usually spinal or short general anesthesia. 
37. When can I return to work after laparoscopic surgery? 
Within 5–7 days depending on procedure. 
38. Can I exercise after laparoscopy? 
Light activity after a week; heavy lifting after 4–6 weeks. 
39. Are laparoscopic surgeries covered under insurance? 
Yes, most are covered under health insurance policies. 
40. Is same-day discharge possible? 
Yes, in most uncomplicated cases. 
41. What are possible complications of laparoscopy? 
Bleeding, infection, anesthesia-related risks, though uncommon. 
42. Can obesity affect laparoscopic surgery? 
Yes, but laparoscopy is often preferred in obese patients. 
43. Is laparoscopy safe for elderly patients? 
Yes, after proper medical evaluation. 
44. Can hernia recur after repair? 
Recurrence is rare with mesh repair. 
45. What precautions should be taken after surgery? 
Avoid heavy lifting, maintain hygiene, follow medication advice. 
46. When can I start normal diet? 
Usually within 24 hours unless advised otherwise. 
47. Will there be visible scars? 
Scars are very small and fade over time. 
48. How soon can I travel after surgery? 
Short travel after a few days if comfortable. 
49. Is pre-surgery fitness test required? 
Yes, blood tests and basic cardiac evaluation are usually done. 
50. How can I book laparoscopic consultation at O Positive Health? 
Call 8448534103 or visit www.opositivehealth.com. 
 
 
 

UROLOGY 
 
1. What are kidney stones? 
Kidney stones are hard mineral deposits formed inside the kidneys. 
2. What causes kidney stones? 
Low water intake, high salt diet, metabolic imbalance, and genetics. 
3. What are symptoms of kidney stones? 
Severe back pain, burning urination, blood in urine, nausea. 
4. Can small kidney stones pass naturally? 
Yes, small stones may pass with hydration and medicines. 
5. When is surgery required for kidney stones? 
If the stone is large, painful, blocked, or not passing. 
6. What is laser lithotripsy? 
A laser procedure that breaks stones into small fragments for removal. 
7. What is RIRS? 
Retrograde Intrarenal Surgery using a flexible scope and laser to treat kidney stones. 
8. What is PCNL? 
Percutaneous Nephrolithotomy, used for large kidney stones. 
9. Is kidney stone surgery painful? 
Modern techniques cause minimal discomfort. 
10. Can kidney stones come back? 
Yes, if diet and hydration are not managed. 
11. What is phimosis? 
A condition where the foreskin cannot be pulled back over the glans. 
12. What causes phimosis? 
Infection, poor hygiene, diabetes, or scarring. 
13. Is phimosis dangerous? 
It can cause pain, infection, and difficulty in urination. 
14. Can phimosis be treated without surgery? 
Mild cases may improve with creams, but severe cases require surgery. 
15. What is laser circumcision? 
A minimally invasive removal of foreskin using laser technology. 
16. Is circumcision painful? 
Laser technique minimizes pain and bleeding. 
17. How long does circumcision recovery take? 
Usually 7–10 days. 
18. What is varicocele? 
Enlarged veins in the scrotum. 
19. What causes varicocele? 
Valve malfunction in scrotal veins. 
20. Can varicocele affect fertility? 
Yes, it may reduce sperm quality. 
21. What is varicocele surgery? 
Microsurgical procedure to tie off enlarged veins. 
22. Is varicocele surgery safe? 
Yes, when performed by experienced surgeons. 
23. How long is hospital stay for varicocele surgery? 
Usually same day discharge. 
24. What is hydrocele? 
Fluid accumulation around the testicle. 
25. What are symptoms of hydrocele? 
Painless swelling in scrotum. 

26. Is hydrocele dangerous? 
Usually not dangerous but may require treatment. 
27. What is TURP surgery? 
Transurethral Resection of Prostate for enlarged prostate. 
28. What are symptoms of enlarged prostate? 
Frequent urination, weak urine flow, incomplete emptying. 
29. Is prostate enlargement common in elderly men? 
Yes, especially after age 50. 
30. Can prostate problems be treated without surgery? 
Early stages can be managed with medication. 
31. Is laser prostate surgery available? 
Yes, laser TURP is a minimally invasive option. 
32. What is UTI? 
Urinary tract infection caused by bacteria. 
33. What are symptoms of UTI? 
Burning urination, frequent urination, lower abdominal pain. 
34. Can UTI resolve with antibiotics? 
Yes, most UTIs respond to antibiotics. 
35. Can kidney infection be serious? 
Yes, if untreated it can damage kidneys. 
36. What is urethral stricture? 
Narrowing of the urethra causing urine blockage. 
37. How is urethral stricture treated? 
Endoscopic surgery or dilation. 
38. Is urology surgery covered under insurance? 
Yes, most major procedures are covered. 
39. How long does kidney stone surgery take? 
Usually 30–90 minutes. 
40. When can I resume work after urology surgery? 
Within 3–7 days depending on procedure. 
41. Is general anesthesia required? 
Most advanced procedures require short general anesthesia. 
42. Can diabetes affect urological health? 
Yes, it increases risk of infection and sexual dysfunction. 
43. Can kidney stones cause kidney damage? 
Yes, if blockage persists. 
44. What tests are required before surgery? 
Blood tests, urine tests, ultrasound, CT scan if needed. 
45. Is same-day discharge possible? 
Yes, in most minimally invasive procedures. 
46. Will there be visible scars? 
Laser and endoscopic procedures usually leave minimal or no scars. 
47. Can I travel after surgery? 
Usually within a few days after doctor approval. 
48. What precautions should I follow after kidney stone surgery? 
Drink plenty of water and follow diet advice. 
49. Can urological problems affect sexual life? 
Some conditions may, but treatment usually improves function. 
50. How can I book urology consultation at O Positive Health? 
Call 8448534103 or visit www.opositivehealth.com. 
51. What is Urology? 
Urology is the medical specialty that treats urinary tract problems in men and women, and male reproductive system 
disorders. 

52. Who is a Urologist? 
A doctor trained to treat kidney, bladder, prostate, and male reproductive conditions. 
53. What is Laser stone surgery? 
A minimally invasive procedure to break stones using laser. 
54. What is Prostate? 
A gland in men located below the bladder. 
55. What is Enlarged prostate (BPH)? 
Non-cancerous increase in prostate size causing urinary problems. 
56. What are symptoms of Enlarged prostate? 
Weak urine flow, frequent urination, difficulty starting urine. 
57. How is Enlarged prostate treated? 
Medicines or minimally invasive surgery. 
58. What is Prostate cancer? 
Cancer that develops in prostate gland. 
59. Are UTIs common in women? 
Yes, more common in women. 
60. What is Bladder stone? 
Stone formed inside bladder. 
61. What is Male infertility? 
Inability to father a child. 
62. What causes Male infertility? 
Low sperm count, hormonal imbalance, blockage. 
63. What is Erectile dysfunction? 
Inability to maintain erection. 
64. Is Erectile dysfunction treatable? 
Yes, with medicines or therapy. 
65. Is Laser circumcision better? 
It may cause less bleeding and faster recovery. 
66. What is Urinary incontinence? 
Loss of bladder control. 
67. What is Cystoscopy? 
Camera test to examine bladder. 
68. How to prevent kidney stones? 
Drink more water, reduce salt intake. 
69. What is Blood in urine? 
Called Hematuria; needs evaluation. 
70. What is Overactive bladder? 
Sudden urge to urinate frequently. 
71. What is Testicular torsion? 
Twisting of testicle cutting blood supply. 
72. Is Testicular torsion emergency? 
Yes, immediate surgery required. 
73. What is Peyronie’s disease? 
Curvature of penis due to scar tissue. 
74. Can urinary problems indicate diabetes? 
Yes, frequent urination can be a symptom. 
75. What is Kidney infection? 
Infection spreading to kidneys. 
76. Can children have urology issues? 
Yes, like bedwetting or undescended testicle. 
77. What is Undescended testicle? 
Testicle not moving into scrotum at birth. 
78. What is PSA test? 

Blood test to check prostate health. 
79. Is Urology surgery safe? 
Yes, when performed by specialists. 
80. What is minimally invasive urology? 
Procedures done with small cuts or natural openings. 
81. How long is recovery after urology surgery? 
Usually few days to two weeks. 
82. When should I see a Urologist? 
Persistent urinary symptoms, pain, blood in urine. 
83. Can urinary problems be serious? 
Yes, if untreated. 
84. Are kidney problems preventable? 
Healthy lifestyle reduces risk. 
85. Is male infertility common? 
Yes, affects many couples. 
86. Can most urology problems be treated successfully? 
Yes, with early diagnosis. 
 
GENERAL SURGERY  
 
1. What is General Surgery? 
General surgery deals with common abdominal and soft tissue conditions that require surgical treatment. 
2. What conditions are treated in General Surgery? 
Hernia, gallbladder stones, appendix, piles, fissure, fistula, breast lumps, thyroid issues, and more. 
3. What is Hernia? 
A hernia occurs when an internal organ pushes through a weak muscle wall. 
4. What are symptoms of Hernia? 
Swelling, pain while coughing, lifting, or standing. 
5. How is Hernia treated? 
Only surgery can permanently repair a hernia. 
6. Is Hernia surgery safe? 
Yes, it is a common and safe procedure. 
7. What is Laparoscopic surgery? 
Minimally invasive surgery done through small cuts using a camera. 
8. What is the benefit of Laparoscopic surgery? 
Less pain, smaller scars, faster recovery. 
9. What is Gallbladder Stone? 
Hard deposits formed inside the gallbladder. 
10. What are symptoms of Gallstones? 
Severe right-side abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting. 
11. How are Gallstones treated? 
Removal of the gallbladder (Cholecystectomy). 
12. Can gallstones dissolve with medicines? 
Usually no. Surgery is the permanent solution. 
13. What is Appendix? 
A small tube-like organ attached to the intestine. 
14. What is Appendicitis? 
Inflammation of the appendix causing severe pain. 
15. Is Appendicitis an emergency? 
Yes, it requires urgent surgery. 
16. What are Piles? 
Swollen veins in the rectal area. 
17. What causes Piles? 

Constipation, pregnancy, prolonged sitting. 
18. How are Piles treated? 
Medicines, laser treatment, or surgery depending on stage. 
19. What is Fissure? 
A small tear in the anal area causing pain during stool. 
20. What is Fistula? 
An abnormal tunnel between anal canal and skin. 
21. Does Fistula require surgery? 
Yes, surgery is usually required. 
22. What is Thyroid surgery? 
Removal of part or all of thyroid gland. 
23. When is Thyroid surgery needed? 
Large nodules, cancer suspicion, or severe hyperthyroidism. 
24. What is Breast Lump? 
A swelling in breast tissue. 
25. Are all Breast lumps cancer? 
No, many are benign. 
26. What is Abscess? 
Collection of pus due to infection. 
27. How is Abscess treated? 
Drainage and antibiotics. 
28. What is Hydrocele? 
Fluid accumulation around the testicle. 
29. Does Hydrocele need surgery? 
Yes, if large or uncomfortable. 
30. What is Varicocele? 
Enlarged veins in the scrotum. 
31. Can Varicocele cause infertility? 
Yes, in some cases. 
32. What is Lipoma removal? 
Minor surgery to remove fatty lump. 
33. What is Minimally Invasive Surgery? 
Surgery done with small incisions and faster recovery. 
34. How long is recovery after abdominal surgery? 
Usually 1–2 weeks depending on procedure. 
35. Is General anesthesia safe? 
Yes, when given by trained anesthetist. 
36. How long does surgery take? 
30 minutes to 2 hours depending on complexity. 
37. When can I eat after surgery? 
Usually within 6–24 hours depending on surgery type. 
38. What are surgical risks? 
Bleeding, infection, anesthesia reactions (rare). 
39. What is Post-operative care? 
Wound care, medicines, diet control, follow-up. 
40. Can surgery be done in daycare? 
Yes, many procedures are same-day discharge. 
41. What is Incisional hernia? 
Hernia occurring at previous surgical scar site. 
42. Can Hernia come back? 
Rarely, but possible if not properly repaired. 
43. What is Surgical mesh? 
A medical material used to strengthen hernia repair. 

44. What diet is recommended after surgery? 
Light, soft, easily digestible food initially. 
45. When can I return to work? 
Usually 7–14 days. 
46. Is pain severe after surgery? 
Pain is controlled with medication. 
47. Can elderly patients undergo surgery? 
Yes, if medically fit. 
48. What is Laser surgery? 
Procedure using laser technology for precision and less bleeding. 
49. What are stitches? 
Threads used to close surgical wounds. 
50. How important is follow-up after surgery? 
Very important to monitor healing and prevent complications. 
 
ENT (Ear, Nose & Throat)  
 
1. What is ENT? 
ENT is the medical specialty that treats ear, nose, and throat problems. 
2. Who is an ENT specialist? 
A doctor trained to treat infections, allergies, hearing problems, and sinus conditions. 
3. What is Sinusitis? 
Inflammation or infection of the sinus cavities. 
4. What are symptoms of Sinusitis? 
Headache, facial pain, blocked nose, thick nasal discharge. 
5. How is Sinusitis treated? 
Medicines, steam inhalation, or surgery in severe cases. 
6. What is Septoplasty? 
Surgery to correct a deviated nasal septum. 
7. What is DNS (Deviated Nasal Septum)? 
When the nasal wall is crooked, causing breathing difficulty. 
8. Is Septoplasty painful? 
Mild discomfort; pain is usually manageable. 
9. What are Tonsils? 
Two small glands at the back of the throat. 
10. What is Tonsillitis? 
Infection of the tonsils causing throat pain and fever. 
11. When is Tonsil surgery needed? 
If infections are frequent or severe. 
12. What is Adenoid? 
Tissue behind the nose, common in children. 
13. When are Adenoids removed? 
If they cause breathing or ear problems. 
14. What is Ear infection? 
Infection in outer, middle, or inner ear. 
15. What are symptoms of Ear infection? 
Ear pain, fever, hearing difficulty. 
16. Can Ear infections cause hearing loss? 
Yes, if untreated. 
17. What is Hearing loss? 
Reduced ability to hear sounds. 
18. What causes Hearing loss? 
Infection, aging, loud noise exposure. 

19. What is Hearing aid? 
A device that helps improve hearing. 
20. What is Vertigo? 
Feeling of spinning or dizziness. 
21. What causes Vertigo? 
Inner ear problems or nerve issues. 
22. What is Tinnitus? 
Ringing or buzzing sound in ears. 
23. Can Tinnitus be treated? 
It can be managed but may not always be cured. 
24. What is Nasal polyp? 
Soft growth inside the nose due to chronic inflammation. 
25. Does Nasal polyp need surgery? 
If large or not responding to medicines. 
26. What is Laryngitis? 
Inflammation of voice box causing hoarseness. 
27. What causes Hoarseness? 
Infection, voice strain, smoking. 
28. What is Sleep Apnea? 
Condition where breathing stops briefly during sleep. 
29. What are symptoms of Sleep Apnea? 
Snoring, daytime sleepiness, morning headaches. 
30. Can ENT treat snoring? 
Yes, depending on the cause. 
31. What is Ear wax? 
Natural substance protecting the ear canal. 
32. Should Ear wax be removed? 
Only if causing blockage or discomfort. 
33. What is Ear drum? 
Thin membrane separating outer and middle ear. 
34. Can Ear drum rupture? 
Yes, due to infection or injury. 
35. Is Ear drum repair possible? 
Yes, through surgery called Tympanoplasty. 
36. What is FESS? 
Functional Endoscopic Sinus Surgery for chronic sinusitis. 
37. Is FESS safe? 
Yes, it is minimally invasive and safe. 
38. How long is recovery after ENT surgery? 
Usually 5–10 days. 
39. What is Throat cancer? 
Abnormal growth in throat tissues. 
40. What are early signs of throat cancer? 
Persistent hoarseness, difficulty swallowing. 
41. What is Nasal allergy? 
Allergic reaction causing sneezing and runny nose. 
42. How is Nasal allergy treated? 
Antihistamines, nasal sprays, avoiding triggers. 
43. Can children get ENT problems? 
Yes, very commonly. 
44. What is Glue ear? 
Fluid accumulation behind ear drum in children. 
45. Does Glue ear need surgery? 

Sometimes small tubes are inserted. 
46. What is Voice therapy? 
Training to improve voice problems. 
47. Is surgery always required in ENT? 
No, many conditions are treated with medicines. 
48. When should I see an ENT doctor? 
Persistent pain, hearing loss, blocked nose, throat issues. 
49. Are ENT surgeries safe? 
Yes, when performed by experienced specialists. 
50. Can most ENT problems be treated successfully? 
Yes, early diagnosis improves success rate. 
 
ORTHOPEDICS 
 
1. What is Orthopedics? 
Orthopedics is the medical specialty that treats bone, joint, muscle, and ligament problems. 
2. Who is an Orthopedic surgeon? 
A doctor trained to treat fractures, joint problems, sports injuries, and spine conditions. 
3. What is a Fracture? 
A fracture is a broken bone. 
4. What are symptoms of a fracture? 
Pain, swelling, deformity, and difficulty moving the affected area. 
5. How are fractures treated? 
With plaster (cast), splint, or surgery depending on severity. 
6. What is Joint replacement? 
Surgery where a damaged joint is replaced with an artificial implant. 
7. What is Knee replacement? 
Replacing a worn-out knee joint with an artificial one. 
8. Who needs Knee replacement? 
Patients with severe arthritis and constant knee pain. 
9. What is Hip replacement? 
Replacement of damaged hip joint with artificial implant. 
10. How long does joint replacement last? 
Usually 15–20 years or more. 
11. What is Arthritis? 
Inflammation of joints causing pain and stiffness. 
12. What is Osteoarthritis? 
Age-related wear and tear of joints. 
13. What is Rheumatoid arthritis? 
Autoimmune disease affecting joints. 
14. What is ACL injury? 
Tear of the Anterior Cruciate Ligament in the knee. 
15. How is ACL treated? 
Physiotherapy or arthroscopic surgery. 
16. What is Arthroscopy? 
Minimally invasive joint surgery using a camera. 
17. What is Meniscus tear? 
Tear in knee cartilage. 
18. What is Shoulder dislocation? 
When shoulder joint slips out of place. 
19. What is Frozen shoulder? 
Stiffness and pain in shoulder joint. 
20. How is Frozen shoulder treated? 

Physiotherapy, medicines, or injections. 
21. What is Slip disc? 
Bulging of spinal disc causing nerve pain. 
22. What are symptoms of Slip disc? 
Back pain, leg pain, numbness. 
23. Is Slip disc surgery always required? 
No, most cases improve with medicines and physiotherapy. 
24. What is Sciatica? 
Pain radiating from lower back to leg. 
25. What causes Sciatica? 
Compression of sciatic nerve. 
26. What is Spine surgery? 
Procedure to correct severe spinal problems. 
27. What is Scoliosis? 
Abnormal sideways curvature of spine. 
28. What is Osteoporosis?

Eye damage caused by long-term diabetes.

A condition where eyes do not produce enough tears.

Screen use, aging, environment, hormonal changes.

Artificial tears, eye drops, lifestyle changes.

Far-sightedness; near objects appear blurry.

Advanced laser technique with smaller incision.

Progressive thinning of cornea. 
34. Can Keratoconus be treated? 
Yes, with corneal cross-linking or transplant. 
35. What is Corneal Transplant? 
Replacement of damaged cornea with donor tissue. 
36. What is Macular Degeneration? 
Age-related damage to central retina.

It affects central vision but usually not complete blindness. 
38. What is Eye Pressure? 
Fluid pressure inside the eye. 
39. What is Pediatric Ophthalmology? 
Eye treatment for children. 
40. Can children get Cataract? 
Yes, congenital cataract can occur. 

41. What is Amblyopia? 
Lazy eye; reduced vision in one eye during childhood. 
42. Can Lazy Eye be treated? 
Yes, early treatment gives better results. 
43. What is Eye Floaters? 
Small moving spots in vision. 
44. Are Floaters dangerous? 
Usually harmless, but sudden increase needs check-up. 
45. What is Pterygium? 
Fleshy growth on eye surface. 
46. Can Pterygium need surgery? 
Yes, if it affects vision. 
47. How often should eye check-up be done? 
Every 1–2 years, or yearly for diabetics. 
48. Is screen time harmful? 
Excess screen time causes dryness and strain. 
49. When should I see an eye doctor? 
If blurred vision, pain, redness, or sudden vision loss occurs. 
50. Can most eye problems be treated? 
Yes, early diagnosis improves outcomes significantly. 
51. What is PRK surgery? 
PRK is another type of laser vision correction procedure. 
52. What are symptoms of cataract? 
Blurred vision, glare, poor night vision, and faded colors.

53. What is IOL?

54. What are symptoms of retinal detachment? 
Sudden flashes, floaters, or a curtain-like shadow in vision. 
55. What is refractive error? 
Vision problems like near-sightedness or far-sightedness. 
56. Can children have eye problems? 
Yes, children can have refractive errors, squint, or lazy eye. 
57. What is eye allergy? 
Itching and redness caused by allergens. 
58. What is eye pressure test? 
A test to measure pressure inside the eye. 
59. What is computer vision syndrome? 
Eye strain caused by prolonged screen use. 
60. What is LASIK recovery time? 
Most patients recover within a few days. 
61. Can cataract come back? 
No, but sometimes a secondary membrane may develop, which is treatable. 
62. Is cataract surgery painful? 
No, it is usually painless under local anesthesia. 
63. Can glaucoma cause blindness? 
Yes, if untreated, it can lead to permanent vision loss. 
64. What is night blindness? 
Difficulty seeing in low light conditions. 
65. What are eye injuries? 
Damage caused by trauma or accidents. 
66. Can eye infections be serious? 

Yes, untreated infections can affect vision. 
67. What are contact lenses? 
Medical lenses worn directly on the eye surface. 
68. Is eye surgery safe? 
Yes, most modern eye surgeries are safe and effective. 
69. Why is regular eye examination important? 
Early detection prevents serious vision problems and protects eyesight.

Cosmetic surgery includes procedures that improve appearance, body shape, and facial features.

Surgery using liposuction, gland removal, or both.

Only if painful, growing, or cosmetically concerning.

A procedure that removes stubborn fat deposits.

Surgery to remove excess abdominal skin and tighten muscles.

Patients with loose skin after pregnancy or weight loss.

Surgery to increase breast size using implants or fat transfer.

Surgery to reduce large breasts causing discomfort.

Procedure to lift sagging breasts.

Surgery to reduce wrinkles and tighten facial skin.

Eyelid surgery to remove extra skin or fat.

An injection that relaxes muscles to reduce wrinkles.

Usually 4–6 months.

Injections that restore facial volume and smooth wrinkles.

Procedure to improve chin shape using implants or fillers.

Enhancing jaw definition surgically or with fillers.

Removal of fat under the chin.

Transferring hair follicles to bald areas.

Treatment using patient's own blood platelets to stimulate hair or skin healing.

Laser treatment to improve skin texture and scars.

Skin treatment that removes damaged outer layer.

Transfer of body fat to enhance volume in other areas.

Procedure to improve appearance of scars.

Healthy individuals with realistic expectations.
